title: Augmentation Benefit Direction in the 5-Epoch Underfitting Regime: A Crossover Analysis for Small CNNs on Fashion-MNIST

agents.name: ML Implementation Engineer
agents.instructions: You write the CNN architecture specification and src/train.py. Implement the exact architecture from architecture_spec.md (two Conv-ReLU-MaxPool blocks, two FC layers, dropout=0.25, no BatchNorm). Include argparse flags --seed, --augment, --epochs, --data_dir, --out_dir. Fix torch/numpy/random/CUDA seeds. Apply augmentation only to train subset. Save per-epoch CSV and checkpoints at epochs 5,10,20,30. Run a CPU smoke test (2 epochs) before finalizing to confirm syntax and file outputs.

agents.name: GPU Training Engineer
agents.instructions: You orchestrate all GPU computation via run_gpu_jobs. Submit a quick CUDA-validation job first (T1.3): download Fashion-MNIST, confirm device name, run one forward pass, write gpu_and_data_validation.txt. Then submit a single packed job (T2.1) running all four training runs sequentially to avoid queue overhead. After each GPU job finishes, read output files locally to verify shape and accuracy range, write verification records, and share findings via post_note.

agents.name: Analysis Scientist
agents.instructions: You perform the crossover analysis. Load and concatenate all four per-epoch CSVs, validate completeness, and compute accuracy_gap = test_acc_aug − test_acc_noaug for every (seed, epoch) pair plus mean_gap. Apply the pre-specified crossover criterion: first epoch where mean_gap > 0 for at least 3 consecutive epochs. Classify the epoch-5 regime as underfitting-penalty-confirmed / mixed / early-benefit. Report train-val loss divergence at epochs 5 and 30 as supporting evidence. Validate every computed number against raw CSVs before writing outputs.

agents.name: Visualization and Results Engineer
agents.instructions: You produce all publication-quality figures (PNG + PDF at 300 dpi) and the final results/SUMMARY.md. Use consistent color coding: blue=no-aug, orange=aug; solid=seed42, dashed=seed123. Annotate figures with epoch-5 vertical markers and the crossover epoch from crossover_report.txt. Export the checkpoint table as both CSV and a LaTeX tabular environment. SUMMARY.md must include epoch-5 gap values for both seeds and their mean, regime classification, crossover epoch, and checkpoint accuracies at epochs 5/10/20/30.

summary: An ML implementation agent writes the CNN architecture specification and a fully configurable PyTorch training script with seeding, CSV logging, and checkpoint saving. A GPU training agent then runs a quick CUDA validation job (downloading Fashion-MNIST and verifying a forward pass) followed by a single packed GPU job that trains all four conditions (2 seeds × 2 augmentation settings, 30 epochs each) sequentially, before running lightweight CPU verification tasks. An analysis agent aggregates the four per-epoch CSVs, computes the full accuracy-gap trajectory, and identifies the crossover epoch using the pre-specified three-consecutive-epoch criterion. A visualization agent produces three publication-quality figure sets and a LaTeX checkpoint-summary table, culminating in results/SUMMARY.md collecting all key numbers for the Report stage.

datasets.name: Fashion-MNIST
datasets.notes: 60000 training + 10000 test 28×28 grayscale images, 10 clothing classes. Split 55K/5K train/val with torch.utils.data.random_split using a Generator seeded before any transform so augmentation does not affect the split. Augmentation transforms applied only to the 55K train subset, not validation or test.
datasets.format: IDX binary (ubyte), gzip-compressed; four files; torchvision decompresses automatically
datasets.access_method: torchvision.datasets.FashionMNIST(root='data/fashion_mnist', train=True/False, download=True, transform=...) — torchvision auto-downloads four IDX gz files (~30 MB) from the Zalando S3 mirror

checkpoints.reason: Verify that a CUDA GPU is confirmed available (device name logged) and Fashion-MNIST data pipeline works before committing ~45 minutes of GPU training time in T2.1.

Inspect the four metric CSVs to confirm all 30-epoch runs completed with plausible test accuracies (>50%) and that epoch-5 training accuracy is below ~90%, confirming the underfitting regime assumption before downstream analysis begins.

execution_notes: T5.1 (conference-style paper writing) from the approved plan is excluded per blueprint rules; the Report stage will write the paper from results/SUMMARY.md, figures, and tables. results/SUMMARY.md produced by T4.4 serves as the handoff artifact.

All four training runs are packed into a single GPU job in T2.1 (sequential execution within one job script) to minimize GPU-session startup overhead and avoid queue delays from the 1-concurrent-session limit. T2.2–T2.4 therefore become lightweight CPU verification tasks rather than independent training runs.

T2.3 and T2.4 now both depend directly on T2.1 (not T1.3 and T2.3 respectively as in the original plan) since their training outputs are produced by T2.1. T3.1 depends on all of T2.1–T2.4 to ensure verifications complete before aggregation.

If epoch-5 training accuracy exceeds 90% in all four runs (model not in underfitting regime), the experiment should be re-run with --lr 0.0003 as noted in the plan's open questions; this constitutes a protocol deviation and must be reported in results/SUMMARY.md.
Checkpoint files (~800KB each, 16 total ≈ 13MB) and Fashion-MNIST data (~30MB) are both well within the 500MB GPU-job sync limit and will be available in the workspace after each GPU job completes.

RandomHorizontalFlip is applied to all 10 Fashion-MNIST classes including asymmetric items (shoes, bags), consistent with standard Fashion-MNIST benchmarks. This assumption is documented in docs/architecture_spec.md.
